title: Create editable terrain
summary: Draw a terrain patch in Top view or convert an existing face or curve.
outcome: You have an editable terrain surface with intentional material and collision settings.

sections.title: Draw a new patch

steps.title: Prepare Top view
steps.text: Choose a material, set the Base height for the new surface, activate Create terrain (T), and set Vertices per side in the Terrain inspector (2 to 16).

steps.title: Draw and inspect
steps.text: Left-drag the footprint in Top view, then check the mesh in Camera and the other grid views. Change the vertex count before drawing if more or less detail is needed.

steps.title: Use it as a room floor
steps.text: Select the new terrain, check Solid collision (players and projectiles) in the Terrain inspector, and click Apply. Build enclosing walls with brushes, leaving a doorway gap. Check the floor's front side and the wall heights in Camera before saving.

tips: Terrain is a surface rather than a closed room. Mesh collision acts from its front side; use closed brushes for walls that must block from both sides.

sections.title: Convert an existing surface

steps.title: Convert a brush face
steps.text: In Face mode select a brush face, choose Vertices per side in the Surface inspector, then click Create terrain from face. The solid brush remains, its source face becomes caulk, and the new terrain inherits texture alignment.

steps.title: Convert a curve
steps.text: Select a curved patch, choose conversion detail in the Geometry inspector, then click Convert curve to terrain. Material, UVs, and vertex color carry over.

tips: Undo restores the original face or curve if the converted surface is not suitable.

sections.title: Continue shaping the mesh

steps.title: Split or stitch
steps.text: For a selected terrain patch, split at an interior row or column. To join adjoining patches, select two whole terrains and use Stitch two patches with a suitable tolerance.

steps.title: Add thickness
steps.text: Use Thicken terrain to add an underside and four walls behind the front surface. Undo removes the shell.

tips: Stitching expects adjoining edges with equal or nested subdivisions; unrelated or distant edges will not join.
